answer: Persistent Attention Ledger gives each identity a rolling score that rises only during unpredictable check-ins; a fable of cheap automation fails when missed windows erase gains. To reach the network's zenith, an identity must answer signed micro-tasks within short random intervals for 30 days, with no gaps. At the summit, each identity costs an attacker roughly 40 hours of real-time monitoring plus proxy and automation fees, and any lapse resets the score.
